items.summary: Carbon-credit methodologies for mangrove restoration typically assume that credited carbon storage persists for a fixed horizon, yet staggered enrollment and unobserved baseline dynamics make permanence risk difficult to identify from satellite time series alone. The framework combines a potential-outcomes model for staggered adoption with a hidden-Markov representation of unobserved baseline loss, and derives bounds on the bias of the conventional permanence deduction. Analysis of the identification conditions shows that the standard deduction is unbiased only when baseline loss is independent of enrollment timing, an assumption that fails whenever enrollment is targeted at high-threat sites. The derived bounds imply that permanence-risk overstatement is increasing in the correlation between enrollment timing and baseline threat, and that the sign of the bias can be recovered from observable enrollment-date and land-cover-covariate patterns. The contribution is a diagnostic that credit issuers can apply to existing registries without new field data, together with a formal statement of the conditions under which the conventional deduction is defensible.

items.summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.

items.summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.

items.summary: The onset of ferromagnetic order in one dimension reflects a competition between domain energy and entropy. For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.

items.summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.

items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

The principal White Rainbow Epoch Hypothesis is deliberately vulnerable to refutation: analysts blinded to point identity must be able to reconstruct an independently calibrated advantage when equally hydrated measurement sites are exchanged under a concealed test condition. Skin water content, contact pressure, temperature, electrode polarization, ordinary neurovascular anatomy, skin pigmentation, photon pathlength and site-selection bias are treated as strong competing explanations, not minor caveats. The civilizational purpose follows a governing three-coupling: Continuity of Chinese Cultural Heritage x Exploration through Modern Science x Original Civilizational Interpretation of the White Rainbow Epoch. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. They are not relabelled novel SI-measurable energy fields or independently validated clinical mechanisms. Established physical laws and metrological statistics likewise remain inherited knowledge rather than purported discoveries by 33 x STARLI. Newly composed, falsifiable interdisciplinary proposals are marked White Rainbow Epoch Hypotheses. Cultural interpretation may remain meaningful even when a particular physical hypothesis fails. The book contains 30 mechanism-distinct golden mathematical plates, 82 scientific chapters and 410 individually paginated research investigations, 200 one-page Research Gates whose large deep-navy opening questions lead to discriminating experiments, and 33 scientifically distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. The Gates present concrete blinded challenges, resource-matched traditional metrology baselines, necessary calibration and acceptance margins, failure pathways and independent handoff requirements. Each Phoenix embryo has a different named instrument or provisional mechanism, adversarial test, rival explanation and honest metamorphosis path when rejected. The project does not exclude established scientific knowledge or ancient philosophy; it simply does not include other authors' DOI records in this particular bibliography.

items.summary: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github
